questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2 'the'** because we use the definite article 'the' when talking about a specific reference. In the passage we are talking about particular 'sacred practices'.
 
• Option 1 is wrong because the article 'a' is used only before consonant sounding words.
 
• Option 3 is wrong because we don't use the numeral 'one' before a plural entity.
 
• Option 4 is wrong because we use the article 'an' only before vowel sounding words.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.solution:

• In this sentence the word 'which' fits the blank correctly as it refers to 'the banana plant' because we use 'which' to refer to animals, plants and things.

• Option 3 is wrong because the pronoun 'whom' is used to ask 'what person or which person'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

They are going to open the shops at eleven o'clock.

options.text: The shops were opened at eleven o'clock.
The shops have been opened at eleven o'clock.
The shops are going to be opened at eleven o'clock.
The shops must be opened at eleven o'clock.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3)

__
 
• we need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an assertive sentence-

 
 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases as well if subject and object are pronouns.
 
• Sometimes we don't write the agency involved, in passive form.
 
 
 
• Generally, **"Sub + is/am/are/was/were/will be/shall be + verb-ing form + other words__" **syntax is used for continuous tenses, but "__Sub + is/am/are/was/were + going + Infinitive (to + ____verb¹) + other words__" syntax is used to refer a time in near future e.g. *I am going to take my lunch.* __(I will take my lunch in some time)__
 __
 
• So we will follow the rule of infinitive verbs to change the given sentence into it's passive form.
 
• Change** "****To + verb¹**__**"** into **"**__**to + be + verb³**__**" **(to be opened).
 
 
 
• At last line up all the remaining parts.

Following these steps, we finally get - *"*__*The shops are going to be opened at eleven o'clock."*__

questions.question: The age of a father is twice the age of his son. Five years ago, the father's age was thrice the age of the son then what is the age of the son now?
questions.solution:
Let the age of a father = 2x

As per the given information,

The age of his son = x

Five years ago,

Age of father = 2x - 5

Age of his son = x - 5

The father's age was thrice the age of the son.

2x - 5 = 3(x - 5)

→ 2x - 5 = 3x - 15

→ x = 10

Hence, the age of his son is 10 years.

questions.question: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 2 : 5. If the first train runs 250 km in 5 h, then the sum of the speeds (in km/ h) of both the trains is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 2 : 5

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of two trains be 2x and 5x

Speed of first train = 250/5 = 50 km/h

⇒ 2x = 50

⇒ x = 25 km/h

The sum of the speeds of both train = 2x + 5x = 7x = 7 × 25 = 175 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 175 km/h.**

questions.question: If x - 1/x = 7, then x³ – 1/x³ is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x – 1/x = 7

**Formula used:**

(a - b)³ = a³ - b³ - 3ab (a - b)

Calculation:

x – 1/x = 7

questions.question: The compound interest on a certain sum of money at 21% for 2 years is Rs. 11,602.5. Its simple interest (in Rs.) at the same rate and for the same period is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

C.I = Rs. 11,602.5, rate = 21%, time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Compound interest = P [(1 + r/100)n – 1]

Where,

P = Principal amount, r = Rate of interest, n = Number of years

**Calculation:**

Compound interest = P × [(1 + r/100)n – 1]

⇒ 11,602.5 = P × [(1 + 21/100)2 – 1]

⇒ 11,602.5 = P × [1.4641 - 1]

⇒ 11,602.5 = P × 0.4641

⇒ P = 25000

Now, 

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (25000 × 21 × 2)/100

⇒ 10,500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.10,500.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Calculation:

⇒ P = (11,602.5/46.41) × 100

⇒ P = 25000

Now, 

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (25000 × 21 × 2)/100

⇒ 10,500

questions.question: The _______ shows all the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can afford at given market prices and within the particular income level.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. __Budget Line__**

 
• The** budget line** shows all those combinations of two commodities that the consumer can buy spending his given money income on the two goods at their given prices.
 
• An** example **to understand this concept - Suppose our consumer has got an income of Rs. 100 to spend on goods A and B. Let the price of the good A in the market be Rs. 20 per unit and that of B be Rs. 10 per unit. If the consumer spends his whole income of Rs. 100 on good A, he would buy 5 units of A; if he spends his whole income of Rs. 100 on good B he would buy 10 units of B. If a straight line joining 5A and 10B is drawn, we will get what is called the **price line or the budget line.**

**​Note: **

 
• **The utility **is a term in economics that refers to the total satisfaction received from consuming a good or service.

The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. __Baldev Singh__.**

__
 
• **Baldev Singh**__ (1902-1961) was the **first Defence Minister** of India at Independence.
 
• He was the defence minister of India from 15.08.1947 to 13.05.1952.
 
• He was born on 11 July 1902 in a Sikh family in the village of Dummna, in Ropar district of Punjab.
 
• He was also an Industrialist and Politician.
 
• He died in 1961.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to cross the English Channel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e.__ Mihir Sen.__**

 
• Mihir Sen is the **first Indian **and also the** first Asian **to cross the English Channel.
 
• He achieved this feat on September 27 in the year 1958.
 
• The English Channel is a part of the Atlantic Ocean that divides the island of Great Britain from Northern France.
 
• The channel has a length of 563 km and a width of 240 km.

questions.question: Who among the following is the longest serving President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Rajendra Prasad.__**

 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the **first president of India.**
 
• He is also the **longest serving president of India from 1950-62.**
 
• A** lawyer by profession**, Dr. Prasad was an influential leader during the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• He served as the **president of the Constituent Assembly** that drafted the first constitution of the Republic of India, which lasted from 1948 to 1950.
 
• He also became the first **Minister of Food and Agriculture in 1946** in the interim national government.

questions.question: The SI unit of radioactivity is ____________.
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• **Radioactivity: **Radioactive decay is the process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by radiation. A material containing unstable nuclei is considered radioactive.
 
• A **radioactive nucleus consists of an unstable assembly of protons and neutrons** which becomes more stable by emitting an alpha, a beta particle, or a gamma photon.
 
• Atoms are radioactive if their nuclei are unstable and spontaneously (and random) emit various particles α, β, and/or γ radiations.
 
• The original unit for measuring the amount of **radioactivity is Curie (Ci) **– first defined to correspond to one gram of radium-226.
 
• 1 curie = 3.7x10¹⁰ radioactive decays per second.
 
• In the International System of Units (SI)** curie has been replaced by becquerel (Bq).**
 
• **1 becquerel = 1 radioactive decay per second = 2.703x10-11 Ci.​**

**​EXPLANATION__:**

 
• **From the above discussion, the SI unit of radioactivity is Becquerel (Bq).**
 
• The correct answer is **option 4.**

questions.question: In 2019, the Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) new commercial arm called NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) was officially inaugurated in the city of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. Bengaluru.**

 
• NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), was officially inaugurated in Bengaluru.
 
• Its main objective is to scale up industry participation in Indian space programs.
 
• It was inaugurated by **ISRO's honorary adviser, Dr.K Kasturirangan in the presence of chairman Dr.K Sivan.**
 
• It was incorporated on March 6, 2019, for commercially utilizing research and development activities carried out by ISRO in the area of space with an authorized **share capital of Rs 100 crore and initially paid-up capital of Rs 10 crore.**

questions.question: Tears in the eyes are produced by which of the following glands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. Lacrimal gland.**

 
• Tear duct and glands, also called** lachrymal, or lacrimal, duct and glands,** are structures that produce and distribute the watery component of the tear film.
 
• Tears consist of a complex and usually clear fluid that is diffused between the eye and the eyelid.
 
• The** mucous layer **helps the tear film **adhere to the eye surface**, while the **lipid layer **serves to **reduce tear evaporation.**
 
• **Diseases **that damage the lacrimal gland, and thus** decrease tear secretion**, can lead to chronic dry eye, which ultimately can threaten vision.

questions.question: The ________ is the longest river in Sri Lanka.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. Mahaweli.**

 
• Mahaweli Ganga river, **(Sinhalese: “Great Sandy River”)**
 
• At 335 km in length, it is **Sri Lanka’s longest river. **
 
• It rises on the Hatton Plateau on the western side of the island’s hill country, flows north through a tea and rubber growing region, and turns east near Kandy.
 
• It then turns north across the lowlands, where it meets its principal tributary, the Amban Ganga.

questions.question: As of April 2019, who is the Chairman of the joint working group of IRDA and NHA, formed to curb fraud in the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e.__ Dinesh Arora.__**

 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** and **the National Health Authority (NHA) **have formed a working group on the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY).
 
• The joint working group, to be chaired by** Dinesh Arora, Deputy CEO of NHA,** will have **10 members** **from both the organizations.**
 
• In six months, it will submit a report on how to detect and deter fraud through a common repository and capacity-building.
